The work of God is to bring to pass our immortality and eternal life.[^note3] But how can trials and suffering—especially suffering imposed by another person’s sinful use of agency[^note4]—ultimately advance God’s work?

The Lord told His covenant people, “I have refined thee … ; I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction.”[^note5] Whatever the cause of your sufferings, your loving Heavenly Father can direct them to refine your soul.[^note6] Refined souls can bear others’ burdens with true empathy and compassion.[^note7] Refined souls who have come “out of great tribulation” are prepared to joyfully live in God’s presence forever, and “God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes.”[^note8]

**Second, Heavenly Father is intimately aware of your suffering.** While in the midst of trials, we can mistakenly think that God is far away and unconcerned with our pain. Even the Prophet Joseph Smith expressed this feeling at a low point in his life. When imprisoned in Liberty Jail while thousands of Latter-day Saints were being driven from their homes, Joseph sought understanding through prayer: “O God, where art thou? And where is the pavilion that covereth thy hiding place?” He ended with this plea: “Remember thy suffering saints, O our God.”[^note9]
The Lord’s answer reassured Joseph and all who suffer:
“My son, peace be unto thy soul; thine adversity and thine afflictions shall be but a small moment;
“And then, if thou endure it well, God shall exalt thee on high.”[^note10]

Many suffering Saints have shared with me how they felt God’s love during their trials. I vividly recall my own experience at one point in my cancer battle when the doctors had not yet diagnosed the cause of some severe pain. I sat with my wife, intending to offer a routine blessing on our lunch. Instead, all I could do was simply weep, “Heavenly Father, please help me. I am so sick.” For the next 20 to 30 seconds, I was encircled in His love. I was given no reason for my illness, no indication of the ultimate outcome, and no relief from the pain. sources.markdown: Sinful uses of agency that cause suffering to others are too many to list but surely include a spouse who commits adultery, a person who abuses a child or an adult, a drunk driver who injures or kills a loved one, or a mass shooter or a terrorist bomber who maims or kills many.

Elder Robert D. Hales taught: “We must develop the ability to have a concern for others while we are suffering. It is a key element in our spiritual growth. As we lose our lives in the service of our fellowmen, we find ourselves” (“[[Your Sorrow Shall Be Turned to Joy — Hales 1983 Oct|Your Sorrow Shall Be Turned to Joy]],” Ensign, Nov. 1983, 66).

See [Philippians 4:13, 19](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/scriptures/nt/philip/4?lang=eng&id=p13,19#p13); [[Alma 26#12|Alma 26:12]]; see also [[2 Chronicles 32#7|2 Chronicles 32:7-8]][[2 Chronicles 32#8|]].

See General Handbook: Serving in The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, [3.5](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/manual/general-handbook/3-priesthood-principles?lang=eng&id=title_number16#title_number16), ChurchofJesusChrist.org.
James E. Faust, “[[Where Do I Make My Stand — Faust 2004 Oct|Where Do I Make My Stand?]],” Ensign or Liahona, Nov. 2004, 21.

This idea is inspired by Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin’s message “[[Sunday Will Come — Wirthlin 2006 Oct|Sunday Will Come]],” Ensign or Liahona, Nov. 2006, 28–30. See also [[James 1#2|James 1:2-4]][[James 1#3|]][[James 1#4|]] (including the Joseph Smith Translation in footnote 2*a*); [[James 5#10|James 5:10-11]][[James 5#11|]].
Russell M. Nelson, “[[Joy and Spiritual Survival — Nelson 2016 Oct|Joy and Spiritual Survival]],” Ensign or Liahona, Nov. 2016, 82.

Twenty years ago, the Apostle Elder Neal A. Maxwell was pondering his painful and ultimately life-ending illness. The Spirit whispered, “I have given you leukemia that you might teach my people with authenticity” (see Bruce C. Hafen, A Disciple’s Life: The Biography of Neal A. Maxwell [2002], 562).

summaries.adult: Elder Perkins shares his cancer journey to illustrate that physical and emotional suffering— from illness, loss, abuse, or unmet dreams—is universal in mortality. He teaches four gospel principles of hope: trials do not signal God's displeasure but refine the soul; Heavenly Father intimately knows our pain; Jesus Christ's Atonement provides enabling power accessed through covenants like baptism, sacrament, and temple ordinances; and joy can be chosen daily by focusing on God's plan. These truths empower enduring trials with strength, empathy, and eternal perspective.
summaries.youth: Tough stuff like sickness, friend drama, family stress, or feeling anxious hits everyone, but God isn't punishing you—trials build your strength and empathy. Heavenly Dad sees your pain, Jesus gives super strength through covenants (like baptism or sacrament), and you can pick joy every day by focusing on Him, even when life hurts.
summaries.children: God knows when you're sick or sad, like when a friend had cancer and felt His love. Jesus helps us stay strong and find happy times, even on hard days.
summaries.new_members: Suffering is part of life but doesn't mean God disapproves—it helps refine your character. Heavenly Father is aware of every pain, and Jesus Christ's Atonement offers strength through covenants made in baptism, sacrament, and the temple. Focus on God's plan of happiness to find joy amid trials.
summaries.non_members: Suffering—from illness, loss, or heartbreak—affects us all, but God loves you and knows your exact pains. Jesus Christ suffered too, so He can give you strength through faith and commitments to live better. Choose joy by focusing on eternal hope, regardless of circumstances.

/2021/10/54dunn.title: One Percent Better
/2021/10/54dunn.speaker: Michael A. Dunn
/2021/10/54dunn.full_markdown:
For more than a century, the national bicycle racing teams of Great Britain had been the laughingstock of the cycling world. Mired in mediocrity, British riders had managed only a handful of gold medals in 100 years of Olympic competitions and had been even more underwhelming in cycling’s marquee event, the three-week long Tour de France—where no British rider had prevailed in 110 years. So sorry was the plight of British riders that some bike manufacturers refused to even sell bikes to the Brits, fearing it would forever sully their hard-won reputations. And despite devoting enormous resources into cutting-edge technology and every newfangled training regimen, nothing worked.

Nothing, that is, until 2003, when a small, largely unnoticed change occurred that would forever alter the trajectory of British cycling. That new approach would also reveal an eternal principle—with a promise—regarding our ofttimes perplexing mortal quest to improve ourselves. So what happened in British cycling that has great relevance to our personal pursuit to be better daughters and sons of God?
In 2003, Sir Dave Brailsford was hired. Unlike previous coaches who attempted dramatic, overnight turnarounds, Sir Brailsford instead committed to a strategy he referred to as “the aggregation of marginal gains.” This entailed implementing small improvements in everything. That meant constantly measuring key statistics and targeting specific weaknesses.
It’s somewhat akin to the prophet Samuel the Lamanite’s notion of “walk[ing] circumspectly.”[^note1] This broader, more holistic view avoids the trap of being myopically fixated on just the obvious problem or sin at hand. Said Brailsford, “The whole principle came from the idea that if you broke down everything you could think of that goes into riding a bike, and then improved it by 1 percent, you will get a significant increase when you put them all together.”[^note2]
His approach aligns well with that of the Lord, who taught us the criticalness of the 1 percent—even at the expense of the 99 percent. Of course, He was teaching the gospel imperative to seek out individuals in need. But what if we applied that same principle to the very sweet and savory second principle of the gospel, repentance? Rather than being stymied by the churn and dramatic swings between sin and repentance, what if our approach was to narrow our focus—even as we broadened it? Instead of trying to perfect everything, what if we tackled just one thing?
For example, what if in your new wide-angle awareness, you discover you have neglected a daily reading of the Book of Mormon? Well, instead of desperately plowing through all 531 pages in one night, what if we committed instead to read just 1 percent of it—that’s just five pages a day—or another manageable goal for your situation? Could aggregating small but steady *marginal gains* in our lives finally be the way to victory over even the most pesky of our personal shortcomings? Can this bite-sized approach to tackling our blemishes really work?
Well, acclaimed author James Clear says this strategy puts the math squarely in our favor. He maintains that “habits are the ‘compound interest of self-improvement.’ If you can get just one percent better at something each day, by the end of a year … you will be 37 times better.”[^note3]
Brailsford’s small gains began with the obvious, such as equipment, kit fabrics, and training patterns. But his team didn’t stop there. They continued to find 1 percent improvements in overlooked and unexpected areas such as nutrition and even maintenance nuances. Over time, these myriads of micro-betterments aggregated into stunning results, which came faster than anyone could have imagined. Truly, they were onto the eternal principle of “line upon line, precept upon precept, here a little and there a little.”[^note4]
Will little adjustments work that “mighty change”[^note5] that you desire? Properly implemented, I’m 99 percent certain they will! But the one caveat with this approach is that for small gains to aggregate, there must be a consistent, day-in and day-out effort. And although we won’t likely be perfect, we must be determined to mirror our persistence with patience. Do that, and the sweet rewards of increased righteousness will bring you the joy and peace you seek. As President Russell M. Nelson has taught: “Nothing is more liberating, more ennobling, or more crucial to our individual progression than is a regular, daily focus on repentance. Repentance is not an event; it is a process. It is the key to happiness and peace of mind. When coupled with faith, repentance opens our access to the power of the Atonement of Jesus Christ.”[^note6]


As to repentance’s prerequisite of faith, the scriptures are clear. All that’s initially required is a mere “particle of faith.”[^note7] And if we can muster this “mustard seed”[^note8] mentality, we too can expect unexpected and exceptional improvements in our lives. But remember, just as we would not attempt to go from being Attila the Hun to Mother Teresa overnight, so too should we reorient our patterns of improvement incrementally. Even if the changes needed in your life are wholesale, begin at a small scale. That’s especially true if you are feeling overwhelmed or discouraged.
This process is not always accomplished in a linear fashion. Even among the most determined there may be setbacks. Having experienced the frustration of this in my own life, I know that it can sometimes feel like 1 percent forward and 2 percent back. Yet if we remain undaunted in our determination to consistently eke out those 1 percent gains, He who has “carried our sorrows”[^note9] will surely carry us.
Obviously, if we are involved in grievous sins, the Lord is clear and unequivocal; we need to stop, get help from our bishop, and turn away from such practices immediately. But as Elder David A. Bednar enjoined: “Small, steady, incremental spiritual improvements are the steps the Lord would have us take. Preparing to walk guiltless before God is one of the primary purposes of mortality and the pursuit of a lifetime; it does not result from sporadic spurts of intense spiritual activity.”[^note10]

So, does this pocket-sized approach to repentance and real change really work? Is the proof in the pedaling, so to speak? Consider what’s happened to British cycling in the past two decades since implementing this philosophy. British cyclists have now won the storied Tour de France an astonishing six times. During the past four Olympic Games, Great Britain has been the most successful country across all cycling disciplines. And in the recently concluded Tokyo Olympics, the UK won more gold medals in cycling than any other country.



Photographs of British cyclists by (clockwise from top left) Friedemann Vogel, John Giles, and Greg Baker/Getty Images


But far outshining worldly silver or gold, our precious promise down our roadway to the eternities is that we will indeed “triumph in Christ.”[^note11] And as we commit to making small but steady improvements, we are promised “a crown of glory that fadeth not away.”[^note12] With basking in that undimmable luster beckoning, I invite you to examine your life and see what’s stagnated or slowed you on the covenant pathway. Then look broader. Seek modest but makeable fixes in your life that might result in the sweet joy of being just a little better.
Remember, David used just one small stone to take down a seemingly invincible giant. But he had four other stones at the ready. Similarly, Alma the Younger’s wicked disposition and eternal destiny were altered by just one simple, salient thought—a remembrance of his father’s teachings about the saving grace of Jesus Christ. And so it is with our Savior, who, though sinless, “received not of the fulness at first, but continued from grace to grace, until he received a fulness.”[^note13]

It is He who knows when a sparrow falls that is likewise focused on the minute as well as the momentous moments in our lives and who is ready right now to assist you in whatever your 1 percent quest is coming out of this conference. Because every effort to change we make—no matter how tiny it seems to us—just might make the biggest difference in our lives.
To this end, Elder Neal A. Maxwell taught, “Each assertion of a righteous desire, each act of service, and each act of worship, however small and incremental, adds to our spiritual momentum.”[^note14] Truly, it is by small, simple, and, yes, even just 1 percent things that great things can be brought to pass.[^note15] Ultimate victory is 100 percent certain, “after all we can do,”[^note16] through the might, merits, and mercy of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. I so testify in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

Even if the changes needed in your life are wholesale, begin at a small scale. That’s especially true if you are feeling overwhelmed or discouraged.

This process is not always accomplished in a linear fashion. Even among the most determined there may be setbacks. Having experienced the frustration of this in my own life, I know that it can sometimes feel like 1 percent forward and 2 percent back. Yet if we remain undaunted in our determination to consistently eke out those 1 percent gains, He who has “carried our sorrows”[^note9] will surely carry us.

Obviously, if we are involved in grievous sins, the Lord is clear and unequivocal; we need to stop, get help from our bishop, and turn away from such practices immediately. But as Elder David A. Bednar enjoined: “Small, steady, incremental spiritual improvements are the steps the Lord would have us take. Preparing to walk guiltless before God is one of the primary purposes of mortality and the pursuit of a lifetime; it does not result from sporadic spurts of intense spiritual activity.”[^note10]

So, does this pocket-sized approach to repentance and real change really work? Is the proof in the pedaling, so to speak? Consider what’s happened to British cycling in the past two decades since implementing this philosophy. British cyclists have now won the storied Tour de France an astonishing six times. During the past four Olympic Games, Great Britain has been the most successful country across all cycling disciplines. And in the recently concluded Tokyo Olympics, the UK won more gold medals in cycling than any other country.
Photographs of British cyclists by (clockwise from top left) Friedemann Vogel, John Giles, and Greg Baker/Getty Images

But far outshining worldly silver or gold, our precious promise down our roadway to the eternities is that we will indeed “triumph in Christ.”[^note11] And as we commit to making small but steady improvements, we are promised “a crown of glory that fadeth not away.”[^note12] With basking in that undimmable luster beckoning, I invite you to examine your life and see what’s stagnated or slowed you on the covenant pathway. Then look broader. Seek modest but makeable fixes in your life that might result in the sweet joy of being just a little better.

Remember, David used just one small stone to take down a seemingly invincible giant. But he had four other stones at the ready. Similarly, Alma the Younger’s wicked disposition and eternal destiny were altered by just one simple, salient thought—a remembrance of his father’s teachings about the saving grace of Jesus Christ. And so it is with our Savior, who, though sinless, “received not of the fulness at first, but continued from grace to grace, until he received a fulness.”[^note13]

It is He who knows when a sparrow falls that is likewise focused on the minute as well as the momentous moments in our lives and who is ready right now to assist you in whatever your 1 percent quest is coming out of this conference. Because every effort to change we make—no matter how tiny it seems to us—just might make the biggest difference in our lives.

To this end, Elder Neal A. Maxwell taught, “Each assertion of a righteous desire, each act of service, and each act of worship, however small and incremental, adds to our spiritual momentum.”[^note14] Truly, it is by small, simple, and, yes, even just 1 percent things that great things can be brought to pass.[^note15] Ultimate victory is 100 percent certain, “after all we can do,”[^note16] through the might, merits, and mercy of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ. I so testify in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

This principle applies to spiritual growth and repentance: instead of overwhelming overhauls, focus on small, consistent changes like reading a few scripture pages daily, compounding like "line upon line" into profound righteousness. With a mustard seed of faith and daily persistence, these efforts unlock Christ's Atonement, bringing joy, peace, and eternal victory.

Ditch the all-or-nothing stress; pick one thing like less scrolling or daily prayer, stick with it, and watch your habits explode into epic personal wins. Small steps with faith crush bad vibes and level you up big time.
summaries.children: Bike racers who always lost got just a tiny bit better each day in little things, and soon they won gold medals everywhere! You can too—try one small good thing daily, like reading a story from God's book, and He'll help you shine.
summaries.new_members: Repentance and growth in the gospel aren't about massive changes overnight but small, steady 1% improvements, like British cyclists who dominated by tweaking everything a bit. Start with one manageable step, such as short daily scripture reading, fueled by a particle of faith in Jesus Christ. Consistent effort opens the Atonement's power, leading to peace and progression on your covenant path.
summaries.non_members: A failing British cycling team became world-beaters by improving every detail—bike, diet, even laundry—by just 1%, proving small habits compound into huge success. Apply this to life: pick tiny daily tweaks in routines or mindset, stay consistent, and reap transformative joy and momentum. It's a simple, proven path to real personal change.

/2021/10/55douglas.title: Facing Our Spiritual Hurricanes by Believing in Christ
/2021/10/55douglas.speaker: Sean Douglas
/2021/10/55douglas.filename: Facing Our Spiritual Hurricanes by Believing in Christ — Douglas 2021 Oct
/2021/10/55douglas.full_markdown:
For the past six years, my sweetheart, Ann, and I have lived in Texas near the Gulf Coast, where some of the largest hurricanes have struck the United States, leaving behind tremendous destruction and even loss of life. Sadly enough, recent months have been no stranger to such devastating events. Our love and prayers extend to all who have been impacted in any way. In 2017 we personally experienced Hurricane Harvey, which dropped record rainfall of up to 60 inches (150 cm).
Natural laws govern the formation of hurricanes. The ocean temperature must be at least 80 degrees Fahrenheit (27 degrees C), extending to 165 feet (50 m) below the ocean’s surface. As wind meets the warm ocean water, it causes the water to vaporize and rise into the atmosphere, where it liquifies. Clouds then form, and winds produce a spiral pattern over the ocean’s surface.

Hurricanes are colossal in size, reaching 50,000 feet (15,240 m) or more into the atmosphere and spanning at least 125 miles (200 km) across. Interestingly, as hurricanes meet land, they begin to weaken because they are no longer above the warm waters required to fuel their strength.[^note1]
You may never face a devastating physical hurricane. However, each of us has weathered and will weather spiritual hurricanes that threaten our peace and try our faith. In today’s world, they seem to be increasing in frequency and intensity. Thankfully, the Lord has provided us a sure way to joyfully overcome them. By living the gospel of Jesus Christ, we are assured that “when dark clouds of trouble hang o’er us and threaten our peace to destroy, there is hope smiling brightly before us.”[^note2]
President Russell M. Nelson explained:
“Saints can be happy under every circumstance. We can feel joy even while having a bad day, a bad week, or even a bad year!
“… The joy we feel has little to do with the circumstances of our lives and everything to do with the focus of our lives.
“When the focus of our lives is on … Jesus Christ and His gospel, we can feel joy regardless of what is happening—or not happening﻿—in our lives.”[^note3]
Just as natural laws govern physical hurricanes, divine laws govern how to feel joy during our spiritual hurricanes. The joy or misery we feel as we brave the storms of life is tied to the laws that God has set. President Nelson has shared, “They’re called commandments, but they are just as true as the law of lift, the law of gravity, [and] the law that governs the heartbeat.”
President Nelson continued, “It becomes a rather simple formula: If you want to be happy, keep the commandments.”[^note4]
Doubt is an enemy of faith and joy. Just as warm ocean water is the breeding ground for hurricanes, doubt is the breeding ground for spiritual hurricanes. Just as belief is a choice, so is doubt. When we choose to doubt, we choose to be acted upon, yielding power to the adversary, thereby leaving us weak and vulnerable.[^note5]
Satan seeks to lead us to the breeding ground of doubt. He seeks to harden our hearts so that we will not believe.[^note6] The breeding ground of doubt can appear inviting because its seemingly peaceful, warm waters do not require us to “live by every word that proceedeth forth from the mouth of God.”[^note7] In such waters Satan tempts us to relax our spiritual vigilance. That inattention can induce a lack of spiritual conviction, where we are “neither cold nor hot.”[^note8] If we are not anchored on Christ, doubt and its allures will lead us away to apathy, where we shall find neither miracles, lasting happiness, nor “rest unto [our] souls.”[^note9]
Just as hurricanes weaken over land, doubt is replaced with faith as we build our foundation on Christ. We are then able to see spiritual hurricanes in their proper perspective, and our capacity to overcome them is enlarged. Then, “when the devil shall send forth his mighty winds, yea, his shafts in the whirlwind, … it shall have no power … to drag [us] down to the gulf of misery and endless wo, because of the rock upon which [we] are built, which is a sure foundation.”[^note10]
President Nelson has taught:
“Faith in Jesus Christ is the foundation of all belief and the conduit of divine power. …
“The Lord does not require *perfect* faith for us to have access to His *perfect* power. But He does ask us to believe.”[^note11]
Since April general conference, my family and I have been seeking to strengthen our faith in Jesus Christ and His Atonement to help us “turn [our] challenges into unparalleled growth and opportunity.”[^note12]
Our granddaughter Ruby has been blessed with a strong, take-charge will. When she was born, her esophagus was not attached to her stomach. Even as an infant, Ruby, with her parents’ help, met this trial with unusual determination. Ruby is now five years old. Though she is still very young, she is a powerful example of not letting her circumstances determine her happiness. She is always happy.
Last May, Ruby faced an additional hurricane in her life with faith. She was also born with less than a fully developed hand that needed reconstructive surgery. Prior to this rather complex operation, we visited with her and gave her a drawing that beautifully depicts a child’s hand warmly holding the hand of the Savior. When we asked her if she was nervous, she replied, “No, I am happy!”

Then we asked her, “Ruby, how is that so?”
Ruby confidently asserted, “Because I know that Jesus will hold my hand.”
Ruby’s recovery has been miraculous, and she continues to be happy. How the purity of a child’s faith contrasts with the foolishness of doubt that can frequently tempt us as we get older![^note13] But we can all become as little children and choose to put aside our unbelief. It is a simple choice.
A caring father diligently pleaded with the Savior, saying, “If thou canst do any thing, … help us.”[^note14]
Jesus then said unto him:
“If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth.
“And straightway the father … cried out, and said with tears, Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.”[^note15]
This humble father wisely chose to trust his belief in Christ rather than his doubt. President Nelson shared, “Only *your* unbelief will keep God from blessing you with miracles to move the mountains in *your* life.”[^note16]
How merciful is our God to place the bar for us at the level of believing and not at the level of knowing!
Alma teaches:
“Blessed is he that believeth in the word of God.”[^note17]
“[For] God is merciful unto all who believe on his name; therefore he desireth, in the first place, that ye should believe.”[^note18]
Yes, in the first place, God desires that we believe in Him.
We face our spiritual hurricanes best by believing in Christ and keeping His commandments. Our belief and obedience link us to power beyond our own to overcome “[whatever] is happening—or not happening﻿—in our lives.”[^note19] Yes, God “doth immediately bless [us]” for believing and obeying.[^note20] In fact, over time our state of being changes to happiness, and “we are made alive in Christ” as we exercise our faith in Him and keep His commandments.[^note21]
Brothers and sisters, may we choose today to “doubt not, but be believing.”[^note22] “The right way is to believe in Christ.”[^note23] We are “graven … upon the palms of [His] hands.”[^note24] He is our Savior and Redeemer, who stands at our very door and knocks.[^note25] In the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

summaries.adult: Spiritual hurricanes—trials threatening faith and peace—are fueled by doubt, much like warm ocean waters power physical storms, but they weaken when we build our foundation on Jesus Christ through belief and obedience to His commandments. These divine laws, akin to natural principles, ensure joy regardless of circumstances, as taught by President Nelson, by focusing our lives on Christ and His gospel. The talk shares the inspiring example of five-year-old Ruby, who faced surgery with childlike faith that Jesus would hold her hand, demonstrating how choosing belief over doubt accesses miracles and transforms challenges into growth.
summaries.youth: Life's spiritual hurricanes—like doubts, peer pressure, or tough challenges—can hit hard and shake your faith, but believing in Jesus Christ and living His gospel gives you unbeatable power to stay happy and strong. Just like little Ruby trusted Jesus to hold her hand through scary surgery and came out smiling, pick faith over doubt to conquer your storms and find real joy no matter what!
summaries.children: Hurricanes are big scary storms, but spiritual storms in life can be scary too. Believe in Jesus, and He'll hold your hand to keep you safe and happy!
summaries.new_members: Spiritual hurricanes are life's trials that test faith, powered by doubt but overcome by believing in Jesus Christ and keeping His commandments, which are divine laws bringing joy like gravity or lift. This focus on Christ ensures happiness amid any storm, as a child's pure faith during surgery shows. Welcome to this joyful path of belief and obedience.
summaries.non_members: Life brings spiritual hurricanes—challenges that threaten peace—but believing in Jesus Christ and following His teachings provides strength and joy, no matter the circumstances. Doubt fuels these storms, while faith, like a child's trust during hardship, connects us to divine power for miracles. It's a simple choice: believe to overcome and find lasting happiness.

topics.name: Physical Hurricanes Analogy
topics.summary: The speaker describes living near hurricane-prone areas, the natural laws governing their formation from warm ocean waters, and how they weaken upon reaching land, setting up a metaphor for spiritual storms.

question_quote_pairs.question: How might recognizing the conditions that fuel physical hurricanes help you identify and avoid the "breeding grounds" for your own spiritual challenges?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "Natural laws govern the formation of hurricanes. The ocean temperature must be at least 80 degrees Fahrenheit (27 degrees C), extending to 165 feet (50 m) below the ocean’s surface."

question_quote_pairs.question: In what ways have your "spiritual hurricanes" weakened when you've moved toward the "land" of Christ's gospel?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "as hurricanes meet land, they begin to weaken because they are no longer above the warm waters required to fuel their strength."

topics.name: Joy Amid Spiritual Hurricanes
topics.summary: Spiritual hurricanes threaten faith and peace but increase in today's world; joy comes not from circumstances but from focusing on Jesus Christ and His gospel, governed by divine laws like keeping commandments.

question_quote_pairs.question: How can shifting your life's focus to Christ bring joy during your current trials?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "The joy we feel has little to do with the circumstances of our lives and everything to do with the focus of our lives."

question_quote_pairs.question: What commandments could you prioritize to invite more joy into a "bad year"?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "If you want to be happy, keep the commandments."

topics.name: Doubt Versus Faith in Christ
topics.summary: Doubt acts as the warm-water breeding ground for spiritual hurricanes, weakening us, while choosing faith in Christ as our foundation replaces doubt, accesses divine power, and enlarges our capacity to overcome storms.

question_quote_pairs.question: When have you chosen doubt over belief, and how did it make you more vulnerable—what can you do differently next time?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "Just as warm ocean water is the breeding ground for hurricanes, doubt is the breeding ground for spiritual hurricanes. Just as belief is a choice, so is doubt."

question_quote_pairs.question: How does imperfect faith still qualify you for Christ's power in your spiritual hurricanes?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "The Lord does not require perfect faith for us to have access to His perfect power. But He does ask us to believe."

topics.name: Exemplars of Childlike Belief
topics.summary: Stories of the speaker's granddaughter Ruby, who trusts Christ amid surgeries, and a biblical father who chooses belief over unbelief illustrate how simple faith leads to happiness, miracles, and growth despite trials.

question_quote_pairs.question: Like Ruby, how can trusting Jesus to "hold your hand" change your approach to personal health or family challenges?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "Ruby confidently asserted, 'Because I know that Jesus will hold my hand.'"

question_quote_pairs.question: When facing doubt in your trials, how can you echo the father's plea to strengthen your belief?

topics.name: Choose Belief and Obedience

/2021/10/56revillo.title: Miracles of the Gospel of Jesus Christ
/2021/10/56revillo.speaker: Carlos G. Revillo Jr.
/2021/10/56revillo.filename: Miracles of the Gospel of Jesus Christ — Jr. 2021 Oct
/2021/10/56revillo.full_markdown:
*Mabuhay*! I bring to you love and warm smiles from the wonderful Saints of the Philippines. This year marks 60 years since the first missionaries arrived in the islands of the Philippines. Today there are 23 missions and more than 800,000 members of the Church in 123 stakes. There are now seven temples in operation, under construction, or announced. This is truly a miracle. We are witnessing the fulfillment of the prophecy in [[2 Nephi 10#21|2 Nephi 10:21]]: “Great are the promises of the Lord unto them who are upon the isles of the sea.”

This miracle is also a fulfillment of the prophecy given in a prayer by then-Elder Gordon B. Hinckley in Manila in 1961. In that prayer, Elder Hinckley stated: “We invoke Thy blessings upon the people of this land, that they shall be friendly and hospitable and kind and gracious to those who shall come here, and that many, yea, Lord, we pray that there shall be [many,] many thousands who shall receive this message and be blessed thereby. Wilt Thou bless them with receptive minds and understanding hearts, and with faith to receive, and with courage to live the principles of the gospel” (dedicatory prayer at American War Memorial Cemetery, Philippines, Apr. 28, 1961).

Beyond the many, many thousands of faithful Latter-day Saints, the miracle of the gospel has brought positive changes to the country and its people. I am a living witness of this. I was six years old when my parents joined the Church in the southern island of Mindanao. At that time, there was only one mission in the entire country and no stakes. I am eternally grateful for my parents’ courage and commitment to follow the Savior. I honor them and all the pioneers of the Church in the Philippines. They paved the way for the succeeding generations to be blessed.
King Benjamin in the Book of Mormon said: “And moreover, I would desire that ye should consider on the blessed and happy state of those that keep the commandments of God. For behold, they are blessed in all things, both temporal and spiritual” ([[Mosiah 2#41|Mosiah 2:41]]).
As we live and obey the principles and ordinances of the gospel, we are blessed, changed, and converted to becoming more like Jesus Christ. That was how the gospel changed and blessed the Filipino Saints, including my family. The gospel is truly the way to a happy, abundant life.
The first principle of the gospel is faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. Many Filipinos have a natural belief in God. It is easy for us to trust Jesus Christ and know that we can receive answers to our prayers.

The Obedoza family is a great example of this. Brother Obedoza was my branch president when I was a young man. Brother and Sister Obedoza’s greatest desire was to be sealed to their family in the Manila Temple. They lived in General Santos City, 1,000 miles (1,600 km) away from Manila. For the family of nine, making the journey to the temple seemed impossible. But like the merchant man who went and sold all he had to buy one pearl of great price (see [[Matthew 13#45|Matthew 13:45-46]][[Matthew 13#46|]]), this couple decided to sell their house to pay for the trip. Sister Obedoza was worried because they would have no home to return to. But Brother Obedoza assured her that the Lord would provide.
They were sealed as a family for time and all eternity in the temple in 1985. In the temple they found joy incomparable—their priceless pearl. And true to Brother Obedoza’s words, the Lord did provide. On their return from Manila, kind acquaintances gave them places to stay, and they eventually acquired their own home. The Lord takes care of those who demonstrate their faith in Him.
The second principle of the gospel is repentance. Repentance is turning away from sin and turning to God for forgiveness. It is a change of mind and heart. As President Russell M. Nelson teaches, it is “doing and being a little better each day” (“[[We Can Do Better and Be Better — Nelson 2019 Apr|We Can Do Better and Be Better]],” Ensign or Liahona, May 2019, 67).
Repentance is a lot like soap. As a young chemical engineer, I worked in a soap factory in the Philippines. I learned how to make soap and the process of how it works. When you mix oils with an alkali base and add antibacterial agents, it creates a powerful substance that can eliminate bacteria and viruses. Like soap, repentance is a cleaning agent. It allows us the opportunity to get rid of our impurities and our old debris so we are worthy to be with God, as “no unclean thing can inherit the kingdom of [God]” ([[Alma 11#37|Alma 11:37]]).
Through repentance we draw upon the cleansing, sanctifying power of Jesus Christ. It is a key part of the process of conversion. This is what happened to the Anti-Nephi-Lehies in the Book of Mormon. They were Lamanites who were so completely converted that they “never did fall away” (see [[Alma 23#6|Alma 23:6-8]][[Alma 23#7|]][[Alma 23#8|]]). They buried their weapons of war and never took them up again. They would rather die than break that covenant. And they proved it. We know that their sacrifice brought miracles; thousands who fought against them threw down their weapons and were converted. Years later their sons, who we know as the mighty stripling warriors, were protected in battle against incredible odds!

My family and many Filipino Saints went through a similar conversion process. When we accepted the gospel of Jesus Christ and joined the Church, we changed our ways and our culture to align to the gospel. We had to let go of wrong traditions. I saw this in my father when he learned of the gospel and repented. He was a heavy smoker, but he threw his cigarettes away and never touched one again. Because of his decision to change, four generations from him have been blessed.

Repentance leads us to make and keep covenants through sacred ordinances. The first ordinance of salvation and exaltation is baptism by immersion for the remission of sins. Baptism allows us to receive the gift of the Holy Ghost and enter into a covenant with the Lord. We can renew this baptismal covenant every week as we take the sacrament. This too is a miracle!
Brothers and sisters, I invite you to bring this miracle into your life. Come unto Jesus Christ and choose to exercise your faith in Him; repent and make and keep the covenants found in the ordinances of salvation and exaltation. This will allow you to be yoked with Christ and receive the power and blessings of godliness (see [[D&C 84#20|D&C 84:20]]).
I testify of the reality of Jesus Christ and that He lives and loves each one of us. I know that His gospel can bring us hope, peace, and joy, not only now, but it will also bless countless others in future generations. That is the reason for the beautiful and warm smiles of the Filipino Saints. It is the miracle of the gospel and the doctrine of Christ. I testify of this in the sacred name of Jesus Christ, amen.

summaries.adult: The talk celebrates the miraculous growth of the Church in the Philippines over 60 years, fulfilling prophecies and transforming lives through the gospel of Jesus Christ. It emphasizes faith, illustrated by the Obedoza family's sacrifice to be sealed in the temple, and repentance as a cleansing agent like soap, enabling conversion as seen in the speaker's father quitting smoking and the Anti-Nephi-Lehies burying weapons. Through baptismal covenants renewed weekly via sacrament, individuals receive blessings of godliness, joy, and eternal families, with an invitation to exercise faith, repent, and yoke with Christ for abundant life.
summaries.youth: Imagine selling your house to chase a forever-family dream, like the Obedoza family did with faith in Jesus—God provided! Repentance is your daily "soap" to ditch bad habits, just like the speaker's dad quit smoking forever, leading to blessings for generations. Live the gospel principles—faith, repentance, baptism—to conquer challenges and find real joy now and always.
summaries.children: The gospel is a big miracle that grew God's Church in the Philippines and made families super happy. One family sold their house to go to the temple, and God gave them a new home because they had faith!
summaries.new_members: Welcome to the miracle of the gospel, which brings blessings like happiness and family unity when we follow Jesus Christ. Start with faith to trust Him, repent daily like using soap to clean your heart, and make covenants through baptism to receive the Holy Ghost. Renew these weekly with sacrament for God's power in your life.
summaries.non_members: The gospel of Jesus Christ works miracles, like explosive Church growth in the Philippines, turning ordinary lives into joyful, blessed ones through simple steps: faith that God answers prayers, repentance to leave bad habits behind, and baptism to start a fresh covenant with God. Real stories show it provides for families and changes hearts forever, offering hope and peace to anyone.

/2021/10/57meredith.title: Look down the Road
/2021/10/57meredith.speaker: Alvin F. Meredith III
/2021/10/57meredith.filename: Look down the Road — III 2021 Oct
/2021/10/57meredith.full_markdown:
When I turned 15 years old, I received a learner’s permit, which allowed me to drive a car if one of my parents was with me. When my father asked if I would like to go for a drive, I was thrilled.
He drove a few miles to the outskirts of town to a long, straight, two-lane road that few people used—I should note, likely the only place he would have felt safe. He pulled over on the shoulder of the road, and we switched seats. He gave me some coaching and then told me, “Ease out onto the road and just drive until I tell you to stop.”
I followed his orders exactly. But after about 60 seconds, he said, “Son, pull the car over. You’re making me nauseous. You are swerving all over the road.” He asked, “What are you looking at?”
With some exasperation, I said, “I’m looking at the road.”
Then he said this: “I’m watching your eyes, and you are looking only at what is right in front of the hood of the car. If you look only at what is directly in front of you, you will never drive straight.” Then he emphasized, “Look down the road. That will help you drive straight.”
As a 15-year-old, I thought that was a good driving lesson. I have since realized that that was a great life lesson as well. Focusing on the things that are most important—especially those things “down the road,” those eternal things—is a key to maneuvering through this life.
On one occasion in the Savior’s life, He desired to be alone, so “he went up into a mountain apart to pray.”[^note1] He sent His disciples away with instructions to cross the sea. In the dark of the night, the ship that carried the disciples came upon a ferocious storm. Jesus went to their rescue but in an unconventional way. The scripture account reads, “In the fourth watch of the night Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea.”[^note2] When they saw Him, they began to fear, for they thought that the figure that approached them was some sort of ghost or phantom. Jesus, sensing their trepidation and wanting to put their minds and hearts at ease, called to them, “Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.”[^note3]
Peter was not only relieved but also emboldened. Ever courageous and often impetuous, Peter cried out to Jesus, “Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water.”[^note4] Jesus replied with His familiar and timeless invitation: “Come.”[^note5]
Peter, surely thrilled by the prospect, climbed out of the boat not into the water but onto the water. While he focused on the Savior, he could do the impossible, even walk on water. Initially, Peter was undeterred by the storm. But the “boisterous”[^note6] wind eventually distracted him, and he lost his focus. The fear returned. Consequently, his faith diminished, and he began to sink. “He cried, saying, Lord, save me.”[^note7] The Savior, who is always eager to save, reached out and lifted him up to safety.
There are a myriad of lessons to learn from this miraculous account, but I will mention three.


Focus on Christ

The first lesson: focus on Jesus Christ. While Peter kept his eyes focused on Jesus, he could walk on water. The storm, the waves, and the wind could not hinder him as long he centered his focus on the Savior.
Understanding our ultimate purpose helps us determine what our focus should be. We cannot play a successful game without knowing the goal, nor can we live a meaningful life without knowing its purpose. One of the great blessings of the restored gospel of Jesus Christ is that it answers, among other things, the question “What is the purpose of life?” “Our purpose in this life is to have joy and prepare to return to God’s presence.”[^note8] Remembering that we are here on earth to prepare to return to live with God helps us focus on the things that lead us to Christ.
Focusing on Christ requires discipline, especially about the small and simple spiritual habits that help us become better disciples. There is no discipleship without discipline.
Our focus on Christ becomes more clear when we look down the road at where we want to be and who we want to become and then make time every day to do those things that will help us get there. Focusing on Christ can simplify our decisions and provide a guide for how we can best spend our time and resources.
While there are many things worthy of our focus, we learn from Peter’s example the importance of always keeping Christ at the center of our focus. It is only through Christ that we can return to live with God. We rely on the grace of Christ as we strive to become like Him and seek His forgiveness and strengthening power when we fall short.



Beware of Distractions

The second lesson: beware of distractions. When Peter turned his focus away from Jesus and toward the wind and the waves that whipped at his feet, he began to sink.
There are many things “in front of the hood” that can distract us from focusing on Christ and eternal things that are “down the road.” The devil is the great distractor. We learn from Lehi’s dream that voices from the great and spacious building seek to lure us to things that will take us off the course of preparing to return to live with God.[^note9]
But there are other less-obvious distractions that can be just as dangerous. As the saying goes, “The only thing necessary for the triumph of evil is for good men to do nothing.” The adversary seems determined to get good people to do nothing, or at least to waste their time on things that will distract them from their lofty purposes and goals. For example, some things that are healthy diversions in moderation can become unhealthy distractions without discipline. The adversary understands that distractions do not have to be bad or immoral to be effective.



We Can Be Rescued

The third lesson: we can be rescued. When Peter began to sink, he cried out, “Lord, save me. And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him.”[^note10] When we find ourselves sinking, when we face affliction, or when we falter, we too can be rescued by Him.
In the face of affliction or trial, you may be like me and hope that the rescue will be immediate. But remember that the Savior came to the aid of the Apostles in the fourth watch of the night—after they had spent most of the night toiling in the storm.[^note11] We may pray that if the help will not come immediately, it will at least come in the second watch or even the third watch of the proverbial night. When we must wait, rest assured that the Savior is always watching, ensuring that we will not have to endure more than we can bear.[^note12] To those who are waiting in the fourth watch of the night, perhaps still in the midst of suffering, do not lose hope. Rescue always comes to the faithful, whether during mortality or in the eternities.
Sometimes our sinking comes because of our mistakes and transgressions. If you find yourself sinking for those reasons, make the joyful choice to repent.[^note13] I believe that few things give the Savior more joy than saving those who turn, or return, to Him.[^note14] The scriptures are full of stories of people who were once fallen and flawed but who repented and became firm in the faith of Christ. I think those stories are in the scriptures to remind us that the Savior’s love for us and His power to redeem us are infinite. Not only does the Savior have joy when we repent, but we receive great joy as well.



Conclusion

I invite you to be intentional about “looking down the road” and increase your focus on those things that really matter. May we keep Christ at the center of our focus. In the midst of all the distractions, the things “in front of the hood,” and the whirlwinds that surround us, I testify that Jesus is our Savior and our Redeemer and our Rescuer. In the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

For example, some things that are healthy diversions in moderation can become unhealthy distractions without discipline. The adversary understands that distractions do not have to be bad or immoral to be effective.
We Can Be Rescued

The third lesson: we can be rescued. When Peter began to sink, he cried out, “Lord, save me. And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him.”[^note10] When we find ourselves sinking, when we face affliction, or when we falter, we too can be rescued by Him.

In the face of affliction or trial, you may be like me and hope that the rescue will be immediate. But remember that the Savior came to the aid of the Apostles in the fourth watch of the night—after they had spent most of the night toiling in the storm.[^note11] We may pray that if the help will not come immediately, it will at least come in the second watch or even the third watch of the proverbial night. When we must wait, rest assured that the Savior is always watching, ensuring that we will not have to endure more than we can bear.[^note12] To those who are waiting in the fourth watch of the night, perhaps still in the midst of suffering, do not lose hope. Rescue always comes to the faithful, whether during mortality or in the eternities.

Sometimes our sinking comes because of our mistakes and transgressions. If you find yourself sinking for those reasons, make the joyful choice to repent.[^note13] I believe that few things give the Savior more joy than saving those who turn, or return, to Him.[^note14] The scriptures are full of stories of people who were once fallen and flawed but who repented and became firm in the faith of Christ. I think those stories are in the scriptures to remind us that the Savior’s love for us and His power to redeem us are infinite. Not only does the Savior have joy when we repent, but we receive great joy as well.
Conclusion

I invite you to be intentional about “looking down the road” and increase your focus on those things that really matter. May we keep Christ at the center of our focus. In the midst of all the distractions, the things “in front of the hood,” and the whirlwinds that surround us, I testify that Jesus is our Savior and our Redeemer and our Rescuer. In the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

summaries.adult: Using a childhood driving lesson—look down the road to drive straight—the speaker illustrates life's need to focus on eternal priorities. From Peter's walk on water toward Christ, he draws three lessons: center on Jesus by remembering life's purpose to prepare for God's presence through daily spiritual disciplines; beware distractions like adversarial lures or excessive good activities; and trust Christ's rescue amid trials or sin via repentance and faithful waiting. He invites intentional focus on Christ as Redeemer for straight-path living.
summaries.youth: Like learning to drive by looking way ahead instead of just the hood, keep your eyes on Jesus and eternal goals to handle life's storms without swerving. Peter walked on water focusing on Christ but sank from wind distractions—social media, peer pressure, or worries can do that too. Call out when sinking; Jesus rescues through repentance or patience, helping you become who God sees in you.
summaries.children: A dad taught his son to drive straight by looking far down the road. Peter walked on water staring at Jesus but sank looking at waves—Jesus grabbed his hand and saved him!
summaries.new_members: Life's purpose is joy and preparing to return to God, so focus on Jesus like Peter walking on water, building habits like prayer and scripture study. Watch for distractions that pull you off course, even good ones without discipline. Christ rescues us in trials through patient faith or joyful repentance, bringing His infinite love and power.
summaries.non_members: To navigate life steadily, focus far ahead on big goals, like a driving tip to look down the road. In a stormy story, Peter succeeded walking toward Jesus until distractions sank him—life's winds like worries or temptations work the same. Help always comes when you reach out, offering rescue, purpose, and joy.

question_quote_pairs.quote: "There is no discipleship without discipline."

question_quote_pairs.question: How does remembering your life's purpose to prepare to return to God influence your choices?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "“Our purpose in this life is to have joy and prepare to return to God’s presence.”"

question_quote_pairs.quote: "Our focus on Christ becomes more clear when we look down the road at where we want to be and who we want to become and then make time every day to do those things that will help us get there."

topics.summary: Distractions, like the wind that caused Peter to sink, pull our gaze from Christ; Satan uses obvious and subtle ones—even good activities in excess—to derail us from eternal purposes.

question_quote_pairs.question: What "less-obvious" distractions in your life might be keeping you from eternal goals?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "There are many things “in front of the hood” that can distract us from focusing on Christ and eternal things that are “down the road.”"

question_quote_pairs.question: How can you apply discipline to prevent healthy diversions from becoming spiritual distractions?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "The adversary understands that distractions do not have to be bad or immoral to be effective."

topics.summary: Jesus immediately rescues us when we cry out amid sinking from trials or sins, though timing may vary; faithful waiting and joyful repentance bring His saving joy and power.

question_quote_pairs.quote: "Rescue always comes to the faithful, whether during mortality or in the eternities."

question_quote_pairs.quote: "I believe that few things give the Savior more joy than saving those who turn, or return, to Him."

question_quote_pairs.quote: "“Lord, save me. And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him.”"

/2021/10/58andersen.title: The Name of the Church Is Not Negotiable
/2021/10/58andersen.speaker: Neil L. Andersen
/2021/10/58andersen.filename: The Name of the Church Is Not Negotiable — Andersen 2021 Oct
/2021/10/58andersen.full_markdown:
In a press conference on August 16, 2018, President Russell M. Nelson said: “The Lord has impressed upon my mind the importance of the name He has revealed for His Church, even The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.[^note1] We have work before us to bring ourselves in harmony with His will.”[^note2]
Two days later, on August 18, I was with President Nelson in Montreal, Canada. Following our member meeting in the impressive Palais de Congrés, President Nelson answered questions from reporters. He acknowledged that it was “going to be a challenge to [reestablish the name of the Church and] undo [a] tradition of more than a hundred years.” But, he added, “the name of the Church is not negotiable.”[^note3]
Seven weeks later, President Nelson spoke in general conference: “The Lord impressed upon my mind the importance of the name He decreed for His Church, even The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. … It was the Savior Himself who said, ‘For thus shall my church be called.’” Then President Nelson repeated, “The name of the Church is not negotiable.”[^note4]


A Good Question

A good question surfaced: Why now, when for many decades we had embraced the nickname “Mormon”? “The Mormon Tabernacle Choir,” the video spots “I’m a Mormon,” the Primary song “I Am a Mormon Boy”?
The doctrine of Christ is unchanging and everlasting. Yet specific and important steps of the Savior’s work are revealed at their appropriate time. This morning President Nelson said, “The Restoration is a process, not an event.”[^note5] And the Lord has said, “All things must come to pass in their time.”[^note6] Now is our time, and we are reestablishing the revealed name of the Church.
The identity and destiny of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints require that we be called by His name. I was recently in Kirtland, Ohio, where the Prophet Joseph Smith, with only a few members of the Church, prophesied, “This Church will fill North and South America—it will fill the world.”[^note7] The Lord described the work of this dispensation as “a marvelous work and a wonder.”[^note8] He spoke of a “covenant [that would] be fulfilled in the latter days,” allowing “all … the earth [to] be blessed.”[^note9]
The words of this conference are being translated live into 55 languages. Eventually, these words will be heard and read in 98 languages in more than 220 countries and territories.

When the Savior returns in majesty and glory, faithful members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints will be among all nations, all people, all races, and all cultures of the world.



The Growing Influence of the Church

The influence of the restored Church of Jesus Christ will not only be upon those who are members of the Church. Because of the heavenly manifestations in our day, because of the sacred scripture restored to the earth and the powerful gift of the Holy Ghost, we will be a shining light on the hill as the somber shades of disbelief in Jesus Christ darken the world. Although many may allow the world to cloud their faith in the Redeemer, we will “not be moved out of [our] place.”[^note10] Christians who are not among our membership will welcome our role and our sure witness of Christ. Even those Christians who have viewed us with skepticism will embrace us as friends. In these coming days, we will be called by the name of Jesus Christ.
Thank you for your noble efforts to advance the true name of the Church. In the conference three years ago, President Nelson promised us “that our rigorous attention to use the correct name of the Savior’s Church … [would bring us] increased faith and access to greater spiritual power.”[^note11]
This promise has been realized by devoted disciples across the world.[^note12]
Brother Lauri Ahola from the eastern United States admits that at times he finds it awkward to share the full name of the Church. But because of the prophet’s counsel, he persists. On one occasion, he was visiting a friend at a church of another faith. Here are his words:
An acquaintance asked, “Are you a Mormon?”
“‘I am a member of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, yes,’ I said. He started asking me several questions, each beginning with: ‘Does the Mormon Church believe … ?’ And each time, I began my answer with the phrase: ‘In the restored Church of [Jesus] Christ, we believe …’
“… When he noticed that I wasn’t accepting the title ‘Mormon,’ he asked me point-blank, ‘Are you not Mormon?’
“So I asked him if he knew who Mormon was—he didn’t. I told him that Mormon was a prophet … [and I was] honored to be associated with [him].
“‘But,’ I continued, ‘Mormon didn’t die for my sins. Mormon didn’t … suffer in Gethsemane or die on the cross [for me]. … Jesus Christ is my God and my Savior. … And it is by His name that I want to be known. …’
“… After a few seconds of silence, [the acquaintance exclaimed], ‘So, you are a Christian!’”[^note13]

Remember President Nelson’s words? “I promise you that if we will do our best to restore the correct name of the Lord’s Church, He whose Church this is will pour down His power and blessings upon the heads of the Latter-day Saints, the likes of which we have never seen.”[^note14]




The Lord Always Opens the Way

The Lord always keeps His promises. He opens the way for us as we do His work.
For years we had hoped to purchase the internet domain sites ChurchofJesusChrist.org and ChurchofJesusChrist.com. Neither was for sale. About the time of President Nelson’s announcement, both were suddenly available. It was a miracle.[^note15]
The Lord has magnified our efforts in revising names that have long been attached to the Church.
Moving forward in faith, the name of the Mormon Tabernacle Choir was changed to The Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square. The website LDS.org, which received more than 21 million visits each month, was transitioned to ChurchofJesusChrist.org.[^note16] The name of LDS Business College was changed to Ensign College. The website Mormon.org was redirected into ChurchofJesusChrist.org. More than one thousand products that had the name “Mormon” or “LDS” attached to them have been renamed. Faithful Latter-day Saints have adjusted their websites, podcasts, and Twitter accounts.

We adopted a new symbol centered in Jesus Christ.
“At the center of the symbol is a representation of Thorvaldsen’s marble statue the *Christus*. It portrays the resurrected, *living* Lord reaching out to embrace all who will come unto Him.
“Symbolically, Jesus Christ is standing under an arch [reminding] us of the resurrected Savior emerging from the tomb.”[^note17]


The typography of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints has been adapted in more than 50 languages. New domain names have been acquired across the world.



Appreciation for the Help of Others

We appreciate the many good and gracious people who have honored our desire to be called by our correct name. I read an article recently that quoted a Catholic cardinal referring to “the Latter-day Saints.”[^note18] As I visited with a leader of a Christian church a month ago in the eastern United States, he referred to the Church in his first reference with our entire name and followed it up more than once with “the Church of Jesus Christ.”
We realized that adding six words to our name would not be ideal for the media, but, as President Nelson foretold, “responsible media will be sympathetic in responding to our request.”[^note19] Thank you for extending to us the same consideration given cultural, athletic, political, or community organizations by using our preferred name.
There will be a few who, hoping to detract from or diminish the seriousness of our mission, will continue to call us “Mormons” or “the Mormon Church.” With courtesy, we again ask the fair-minded of the media to honor our desire to be called by our name of nearly 200 years.



The Courage of the Latter-day Saints

There are thousands and thousands of Latter-day Saints who have courageously proclaimed the name of the Church. As we do our part, others will follow. I love this story from Tahiti.
Ten-year-old Iriura Jean resolved to follow the counsel of President Nelson.
“In her school class they discussed their weekend … and Iriura talked about … church.
“Her teacher, Vaite Pifao, said, ‘Oh, so you are a Mormon?’
“Iriura stated boldly, ‘No, … I am a member of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints!’
“Her teacher replied, ‘Yes, … you are a Mormon.’
“Iriura insisted, ‘No teacher, I am a member of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints!’
“Ms. Pifao was amazed at Iriura’s conviction and wondered why she was so insistent on using [the] long name of her church. [She decided to learn more about the Church.]
“[Later, as Sister] Vaite Pifao was baptized [she expressed gratitude] that Iriura heeded the counsel of President Nelson.”[^note20]

“The name of the Church is not negotiable.” Let us go forward in faith. When we willingly follow the counsel of the Lord as revealed through His living prophet, especially if it runs counter to our initial thinking, requiring humility and sacrifice, the Lord blesses us with additional spiritual power and sends His angels to support us and stand by us.[^note21] We receive the Lord’s affirmation and His approval.
I am an eyewitness to the power of heaven that rests upon our beloved prophet, President Russell M. Nelson. His most sincere desire is to please the Lord and bless our Heavenly Father’s children. From sacred, personal experience, I testify of the Lord’s love for him. He is the prophet of God.
I witness that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God. In the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

summaries.adult: President Nelson declared the full name of the Church, The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, non-negotiable, as revealed by the Lord, urging members to abandon long-used nicknames like "Mormon" during this phase of the ongoing Restoration. Elder Andersen highlights the Church's global growth and destiny tied to Christ's name, sharing stories like a member's conversation affirming their Christianity and a girl's boldness leading to her teacher's baptism. Practical changes include new websites, a Christ-centered symbol, and renamed entities, with promises of increased spiritual power, miracles, and broader acceptance as faithful witnesses of Jesus Christ.
summaries.youth: Ever feel weird correcting friends who call you "Mormon" instead of saying The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints? Like 10-year-old Iriura, who boldly told her teacher the full name and helped her get baptized—sticking to it shows you're all about Jesus and brings real spiritual power! Our prophet promises blessings when we do this, even if it's awkward at school or online.
summaries.children: Jesus said His Church should be called The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. A brave girl told her teacher the real name, and the teacher learned more and joined the Church!
summaries.new_members: Welcome to The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints—our full name honors Jesus as its head, as He revealed it. We've stepped away from nicknames like "Mormon" to clearly show our Christian faith during this time of growth. Using the correct name invites blessings, deeper power, and helps others understand who we are.
summaries.non_members: Members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints now emphasize their full name to center their identity on Jesus Christ, moving beyond the "Mormon" nickname used for generations. This reflects their global mission and devotion, with stories showing how it sparks positive faith conversations and recognition as Christians. Their prophet promises spiritual blessings for this effort.

topics.name: President Nelson's Directive on the Church Name
topics.summary: President Nelson, inspired by the Lord, emphasizes restoring the full revealed name, The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, declaring it non-negotiable despite longstanding nicknames.

question_quote_pairs.question: How can prioritizing the Lord's revealed name strengthen your personal witness of Jesus Christ?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "The Lord has impressed upon my mind the importance of the name He has revealed for His Church, even The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints."

question_quote_pairs.question: In what situations might you need to affirm that the Church's name is non-negotiable, and how would that build your faith?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "the name of the Church is not negotiable."

topics.name: Why Now? Timing and Church Destiny
topics.summary: Though the doctrine of Christ is unchanging, the Restoration unfolds progressively; now is the time to use the full name as the Church's global identity and prophesied destiny expand to bless all nations.

question_quote_pairs.question: How does recognizing the Restoration as an ongoing process help you embrace prophetic counsel like using the Church's full name?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "The Restoration is a process, not an event."

question_quote_pairs.question: How can being called by Christ's name influence your sense of purpose in the Church's worldwide mission?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "The identity and destiny of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints require that we be called by His name."

topics.name: Growing Influence and Blessings from Obedience
topics.summary: Using the correct name invites greater spiritual power and positions the Church as a light amid global disbelief, as seen in personal stories like Brother Ahola's conversation affirming Christ-centered identity.

question_quote_pairs.question: How have blessings from obeying counsel on the Church's name increased your spiritual power?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "our rigorous attention to use the correct name of the Savior’s Church … [would bring us] increased faith and access to greater spiritual power."

question_quote_pairs.question: When sharing your faith, how can redirecting focus to Jesus Christ, as in this story, open hearts to the gospel?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "‘So, you are a Christian!’"

topics.name: The Lord Opens the Way for Change
topics.summary: The Lord fulfills promises by enabling miracles like domain acquisitions, name revisions (e.g., Tabernacle Choir, Ensign College), and a new Christ-centered symbol across languages.

question_quote_pairs.question: How have you seen the Lord open ways when you've acted in faith on prophetic guidance?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "The Lord always keeps His promises. He opens the way for us as we do His work."

question_quote_pairs.question: What does this Christ-centered symbol inspire you to do in drawing closer to the Savior?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "At the center of the symbol is a representation of Thorvaldsen’s marble statue the Christus. It portrays the resurrected, living Lord reaching out to embrace all who will come unto Him."

topics.name: Courage, Appreciation, and Testimony
topics.summary: Gratitude extends to allies using the correct name; courageous members like young Iriura exemplify bold obedience, leading to baptisms and divine power, culminating in testimony of the prophet and Christ.

question_quote_pairs.question: How can showing appreciation and courtesy to others encourage them to honor the Church's name in your interactions?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "We appreciate the many good and gracious people who have honored our desire to be called by our correct name."

question_quote_pairs.question: What personal courage will you draw from stories like Iriura's to proclaim the full name?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "‘No teacher, I am a member of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints!’"

question_quote_pairs.question: How does following a living prophet, even counter to initial feelings, bring heavenly approval in your life?
question_quote_pairs.quote: "When we willingly follow the counsel of the Lord as revealed through His living prophet ... the Lord blesses us with additional spiritual power and sends His angels to support us."

/2021/10/59nelson.title: Make Time for the Lord
/2021/10/59nelson.speaker: Russell M. Nelson
/2021/10/59nelson.filename: Make Time for the Lord — Nelson 2021 Oct
/2021/10/59nelson.full_markdown:
My dear brothers and sisters, for two days we have been well taught by servants of the Lord who have sought diligently to know what He would have them say.
We have been given our charge for the next six months. Now the question is, how will we be different because of what we have heard and felt?
The pandemic has demonstrated how quickly life can change, at times from circumstances beyond our control. However, there are many things we *can* control. We set our own priorities and determine how we use our energy, time, and means. We decide how we will treat each other. We choose those to whom we will turn for truth and guidance.
The voices and pressures of the world are engaging and numerous. But too many voices are deceptive, seductive, and can pull us off the covenant path. To avoid the inevitable heartbreak that follows, I plead with you today to counter the lure of the world by making time for the Lord in your life—each and every day.
If most of the information you get comes from social or other media, your ability to hear the whisperings of the Spirit will be diminished. If you are not also seeking the Lord through daily prayer and gospel study, you leave yourself vulnerable to philosophies that may be intriguing but are not true. Even Saints who are otherwise faithful can be derailed by the steady beat of Babylon’s band.
My brothers and sisters, I plead with you to make time for the Lord! Make your own spiritual foundation firm and able to stand the test of time by doing those things that allow the Holy Ghost to be with you* always*.
Never underestimate the profound truth that “the Spirit speaketh … of things as they *really* are, and of things as they *really* will be.”[^note1] “It will show unto you all things what ye should do.”[^note2]
Nothing invites the Spirit more than fixing your focus on Jesus Christ. Talk of Christ, rejoice in Christ, feast upon the words of Christ, and press forward with steadfastness in Christ.[^note3] Make your Sabbath a delight as you worship Him, partake of the sacrament, and keep His day holy.[^note4]
As I emphasized this morning, please make time for the Lord in His holy house. Nothing will strengthen your spiritual foundation like temple service and temple worship.
We thank all who are working on our new temples. They are being built all over the world. Today I am pleased to announce our plans to build more temples at or near the following locations: Kaohsiung, Taiwan; Tacloban, Philippines; Monrovia, Liberia; Kananga, Democratic Republic of the Congo; Antananarivo, Madagascar; Culiacán, Mexico; Vitória, Brazil; La Paz, Bolivia; Santiago West, Chile; Fort Worth, Texas; Cody, Wyoming; Rexburg North, Idaho; Heber Valley, Utah; and reconstruction of the Provo Utah Temple after the Orem Utah Temple is dedicated.
I love you, dear brothers and sisters. The Lord knows you and loves you. He is your Savior and your Redeemer. He leads and guides His Church. He will lead and guide *you* in your personal life if you will *make time for Him* in your life—each and every day.
May God be with you until we meet again, I pray in the sacred name of Jesus Christ, amen.

summaries.adult: Amid rapid life changes and deceptive worldly voices amplified by media, we control our priorities and must daily make time for the Lord through prayer, gospel study, focusing on Jesus Christ, Sabbath worship, and temple service to invite the constant companionship of the Holy Ghost and build an unshakeable spiritual foundation. This counters seductive distractions, reveals truth as things "really are," and ensures divine guidance. President Nelson announced new temples in 14 locations worldwide to facilitate this worship.
summaries.youth: Social media and peer pressure can drown out God's voice, but you can fight back by carving out daily time for prayer, scriptures, Jesus-focused worship, and temple visits—like charging your spiritual phone to stay strong against distractions. This builds a foundation that lasts, with cool new temples coming to help you connect with God wherever you are.
summaries.children: Life can change fast, so make time every day to pray, read about Jesus, go to church, and visit the temple. This lets God's Spirit guide you like a best friend, keeping you safe and happy.
summaries.new_members: Welcome to a faith where daily time with the Lord—through prayer, studying Jesus Christ's teachings, Sabbath worship, and temple attendance—invites the Holy Ghost to guide you amid worldly confusions. This strengthens your spiritual foundation and reveals eternal truths. We're building more temples worldwide to make this accessible for all.
summaries.non_members: In a fast-changing world full of competing voices, prioritizing daily time with God via prayer, reflection on Jesus's life and words, worship, and visits to sacred spaces like temples helps discern truth, build inner strength, and receive personal guidance. This simple practice counters distractions and fosters lasting peace.

topics.summary: Though life changes rapidly beyond our control, we can choose priorities, time usage, relationships, and truth sources; counter deceptive media and philosophies through daily prayer and gospel study to hear the Spirit.

question_quote_pairs.question: How can reducing reliance on social media improve your ability to hear the Spirit?

question_quote_pairs.question: What daily habits will protect you from intriguing but untrue philosophies?

topics.name: Inviting the Holy Ghost Daily
topics.summary: Make time for the Lord every day to build a firm spiritual foundation and ensure the Holy Ghost is always present, as the Spirit reveals eternal truths and guides actions.

question_quote_pairs.question: What steps can you take daily to ensure the Holy Ghost is always with you?

topics.name: Centering on Christ and Temples
topics.summary: Focus on Jesus Christ through worship, Sabbath observance, and temple service to invite the Spirit and strengthen foundations; new temples are being built worldwide, with the promise of personal guidance by making time for the Lord daily.
